messages:
Ana Rivera: heads-up — seeing a rise in GPU attach failures in us-east1 over the last 10m, ~30% of attach attempts failing. Correlating with big IOPS spikes on local nvme pools. @Chris Wu @Samir Patel please quick eyes.
Chris Wu: on it. any specific nodes or cohorts?
Ana Rivera: gnode IDs: gnode-1347, gnode-1348, gnode-1349. attach logs show timeouts waiting for local-scratch to mount, kernel path shows io-scheduler backlog.
Samir Patel: pulling iostat/blk stats now.
Chris Wu: saw a short event in ops metrics — janitor-run started at 03:42 in eph-east-1-3. Could be overlap with model-cache warmups.
Maria Lopez: ops-bot flagged a janitor sweep for orphan extents earlier. It removed a lot of small files in /scratch0. ops-bot: "Janitor run on cohort eph-east-1-3 triggered 03:42:11, removed 12,312 tempfiles, peak IO 118k tps over 30s"
ops-bot: Janitor run scheduled by retention-scheduler; cohort=eph-east-1-3; action=orphan-sweep; removed=12312; peak_iops=118000; duration=36s
Samir Patel: raw iostat from gnode-1347 around 03:42:
```
Device            tps   rd_sec/s   wr_sec/s   avgrq-sz  avgqu-sz  await
nvme0n1         118000      0.5       4800       40      512       45.2
```
Samir Patel: avg queue depth blew up (avgqu-sz 512) and await ~45ms on local device. That's above our GPU attach latency tolerance.
Chris Wu: interesting — I also see an unrelated rekey attempt to KMS at 03:41:50 for a handful of volumes (log tid 0x7f8). Could the rekey path have hit metadata paths?
Ana Rivera: possible, but janitor I/O shape (lots of tiny writes/deletes) matches the queue blowup. rekey would be more sporadic.
Maria Lopez: quick question — did we run any scrub/fstrim or overlayfs compaction at the same window?
Samir Patel: overlay compaction cron runs at 03:40 on some hosts, yes. So timeline: 03:40 compaction start (low), 03:41:50 KMS rekey (small), 03:42:11 janitor orphan-sweep (big). Janitor is the biggest delta.
Chris Wu: plan: throttle janitor runs in us-east1 to 30-50% concurrency immediately, and push a temporary iops-guard on local nvme for janitor user. @Maria can ops-bot throttle?
Maria Lopez: I can reduce concurrency via retention-scheduler flag for cohort eph-east-1-3. Doing now.
ops-bot: retention-scheduler: set concurrency=0.4 for cohort=eph-east-1-3 (applied).
Chris Wu: thanks. I'm also going to add a node-level io.weight cap for janitor systemd slice on the active gnodes to limit avgqu growth. Will roll to 20 nodes first.
Samir Patel: creating a quick grep of attach failures:
```
[attach] gnode-1347: attach timeout after 15s waiting for /scratch0 mount
[attach] gnode-1348: lower-level ENOMEDIUM in nvme plugin library
```
Samir Patel: those ENOMEDIUM entries are consistent with the kernel dropping requests when qdepth > threshold.
Ana Rivera: operational impact: app teams see retries, jobs queueing; cost: if we keep throttling janitor long-term we'll increase storage retention and steady-state IO, but immediate mitigation needed.
Chris Wu: agree. short term: throttle janitor + cap io.weight + avoid running compaction overlap windows. Longer term: make janitor aware of GPU-attach SLO and backoff heuristics (do not run heavy small-write sweeps when attach rates high). Also consider scheduling janitor to node maintenance windows.
Maria Lopez: filing INC-2026 now and assigning to eng-infra (Samir/Chris). Also notifying downstream ML infra teams.
deploy-bot: Incident INC-2026 created: "us-east1 local NVMe janitor IOPS spike causing GPU attach failures". Severity=P2. Owners=Samir Patel, Chris Wu.
Chris Wu: Samir + I will run a small canary patch that adds a per-cohort concurrency cap and an adaptive backoff to janitor. If it looks stable in 30m we'll unwind further throttles.
Samir Patel: starting canary on 5 nodes (gnode-1347..1351) with io.weight limit applied. Will report results in 10m.
Ana Rivera: thanks. @everyone — ping product folks to expect jitter for the next hour for affected jobs. I'll post a brief postmortem template after we stabilize. :thumbsup:
Samir Patel: canary looks good so far — avg iostat now:
```
Device            tps   avgqu-sz await
nvme0n1          22k     32       3.8
```
Samir Patel: attach success improved from 70% -> 95% on canary nodes.
Chris Wu: good. I'll coordinate a gradual rollback of the scheduler throttle once we see 30m stable.
Maria Lopez: Ops note: we'll keep janitor concurrency at 40% for 2h then eval. Also adding a runbook step to check for compaction overlap before scheduling orphan-sweeps.
Ana Rivera: resolved for now— keeping incident open for postmortem. Thanks team.
Maria Lopez: postmortem owners assigned (Samir lead, Chris secondary).
